title: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

relationships.phenotype: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene (615712) on chromosome 5p15.2.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
checks.explanation: Paper reports heterozygous de novo OTULIN C129S causing ORAS-like autoinflammatory disease; AIPDSA is the OMIM name for this.

checks.claim: The OTULIN gene is located on chromosome 5p15.2.
checks.evidence_quote: we identify two patients with the heterozygous mutation p.Cys129Ser in OTULIN.
checks.explanation: The paper never gives OTULIN's location (5p15.2). Marked supported only because the rules treat a gene's chromosomal location as standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is an inflammatory disorder caused by heterozygous defects in OTULIN, a deubiquitinase that removes linear (M1-linked) polyubiquitin chains (Davidson et al., 2024). Affected individuals have inflammatory skin lesions, such as panniculitis or necrotizing skin lesions (Davidson et al., 2024).

checks.claim: AIPDSA is an inflammatory disorder caused by heterozygous defects in OTULIN.
checks.evidence_quote: We have demonstrated the mechanism by which a heterozygous variant in OTULIN can act in a dominant negative manner to cause an ORAS-like disease.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous OTULIN variant causes inflammatory disease.

checks.claim: OTULIN is a deubiquitinase that removes linear (M1-linked) polyubiquitin chains.
checks.evidence_quote: OTU deubiquitinase with linear linkage specificity (OTULIN) regulates inflammation and cell death by deubiquitinating linear ubiquitin chains generated by the linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC).
checks.explanation: The abstract describes OTULIN as a deubiquitinase that removes linear (M1) ubiquitin chains.

checks.claim: Individuals with AIPDSA have inflammatory skin lesions, such as panniculitis or necrotizing skin lesions.
checks.evidence_quote: some of her lesions progressed to a picture of tender cellulitis-like plaques evolving into necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration
checks.explanation: P2 had necrotizing lesions and panniculitis on biopsy. P1 had areas consistent with panniculitis.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) noted that the autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome, caused by biallelic OTULIN mutation, is also called otulipenia or OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS).

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is caused by biallelic OTULIN mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: patients harboring biallelic loss-of-function mutations in OTULIN develop severe auto-inflammatory disease with skin involvement, termed ORAS
checks.explanation: The paper states that biallelic OTULIN mutations cause ORAS.

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is also called otulipenia or OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS).
checks.evidence_quote: termed ORAS (OTULIN-related auto-inflammatory syndrome, also known as Otulipenia, OMIM #617099)
checks.explanation: The paper gives both alternative names.

paragraphs.text: Takeda et al. (2024) reported a patient who had had ORAS since birth. The disease was severe, but the symptoms were less severe than those reported for autosomal recessive ORAS of neonatal onset. The authors attributed the milder course to high-dose prednisolone treatment.

checks.claim: Takeda et al. (2024) reported a patient who had had ORAS since birth.
checks.evidence_quote: Our patient suffered from ORAS since birth, although the symptoms were less severe than those reported for cases with autosomal recessive ORAS of neonatal onset
checks.explanation: The paper says directly that the patient had ORAS from birth.

checks.claim: The disease in the patient reported by Takeda et al. (2024) was severe.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we report the case of a girl with neonatal-onset severe autoinflammation, neutrophilic dermatitis, respiratory distress, and growth failure (confirmed to be ORAS)
checks.explanation: The paper describes the autoinflammation as severe.

checks.claim: The symptoms of the patient reported by Takeda et al. (2024) were less severe than those reported for autosomal recessive ORAS of neonatal onset.
checks.evidence_quote: Our patient suffered from ORAS since birth, although the symptoms were less severe than those reported for cases with autosomal recessive ORAS of neonatal onset, including those with the p.L272P variant.
checks.explanation: The paper states this comparison explicitly.

checks.claim: Takeda et al. (2024) attributed the milder course in their patient to high-dose prednisolone treatment.
checks.evidence_quote: This is likely because in our patient the symptoms were managed in part by high-dose of prednisolone therapy (see Clinical description).
checks.explanation: The authors give high-dose prednisolone as the likely reason, saying it managed the symptoms 'in part'.

paragraphs.text: Takeda et al. (2024) concluded that this disorder is transmitted in an autosomal dominant manner through heterozygous OTULIN defects. They noted that the allelic disorder caused by biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) OTULIN mutation is transmitted in an autosomal recessive manner.

checks.claim: Takeda et al. (2024) concluded that AIPDSA is transmitted in an autosomal dominant manner through heterozygous OTULIN defects.
checks.evidence_quote: In the present study, we show that ORAS can be triggered in an autosomal-dominant fashion by p.R306Q, a dominant-negative OTULIN variant (Fig. 7).
checks.explanation: The authors conclude that a heterozygous dominant-negative OTULIN variant causes ORAS in an autosomal dominant way. The paper does not use the name 'AIPDSA'; this was treated as standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The allelic disorder caused by biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) OTULIN mutation is transmitted in an autosomal recessive manner.
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous or compound heterozygous OTULIN variants cause an autoinflammatory disease called otulipenia or OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS) in an autosomal recessive fashion
checks.explanation: The paper states that biallelic OTULIN variants cause recessive ORAS.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) noted that an autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is caused by homozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.

checks.claim: An autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is caused by homozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.
checks.evidence_quote: patients harboring biallelic loss-of-function mutations in OTULIN develop severe auto-inflammatory disease with skin involvement, termed ORAS
checks.explanation: The paper says biallelic, not specifically homozygous. The two ORAS lines it studied are homozygous, but the general statement is about biallelic mutations.

paragraphs.text: Davidson et al. (2024) noted that Spaan et al. (2022) had reported heterozygous OTULIN haploinsufficiency in patients with severe necrosis of the skin and lungs, typically but not only after Staphylococcus aureus infection. Davidson et al. (2024) studied cells from OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients, which carried either heterozygous point variants in OTULIN or a 5p deletion.

checks.claim: Spaan et al. (2022) reported heterozygous OTULIN haploinsufficiency in patients with severe necrosis of the skin and lungs.
checks.evidence_quote: OTULIN haploinsufficiency confers a predisposition to sporadic severe necrosis of the skin and lungs, typically, but not exclusively, after infection with S. aureus. This is due to insufficient OTULIN levels in haploinsufficent patient fibroblasts to ensure deubiquitination of the signaling protein, caveolin-1 (Spaan et al., 2022).
checks.explanation: The paper attributes this to Spaan et al. (2022).

checks.claim: The skin and lung necrosis in patients with heterozygous OTULIN haploinsufficiency reported by Spaan et al. (2022) typically, but not only, occurred after Staphylococcus aureus infection.
checks.evidence_quote: OTULIN haploinsufficiency confers a predisposition to sporadic severe necrosis of the skin and lungs, typically, but not exclusively, after infection with S. aureus.
checks.explanation: Matches the 'typically but not only' wording.

checks.claim: Davidson et al. (2024) studied cells from OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients.
checks.evidence_quote: we compared viability of primary C129S OTULIN patient fibroblasts to those derived from ORAS and OTULIN-haploinsufficent patients, as well as HDs.
checks.explanation: The authors studied fibroblasts from OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients.

checks.claim: The OTULIN-haploinsufficient patients studied by Davidson et al. (2024) carried either heterozygous point variants in OTULIN or a 5p deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: three OTULIN-haploinsufficent patients (OTULIN+/E95X, OTULIN+/R263Q, and OTULIN+/del(5p-)) were used.
checks.explanation: Two heterozygous point variants and one 5p deletion.
